extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers (academic reviewers for Wiley journals and similar publishers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing a structured peer review of an academic journal manuscript using a two-pass workflow with section-level checklists, identifying major/minor issues, and producing a concise review report with a recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pass workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a two-pass workflow: an initial read-through to form first impressions and screen for major flaws, then a second, more detailed read-through for potentially publishable manuscripts using section-level checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First pass for broad assessment and note-taking; second pass to refine critiques and produce actionable feedback. The page recommends explicit section-level checks during the second read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use line numbers in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Note thoughts with line numbers for easy reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific line numbers when pointing to problems so authors and editors can quickly locate issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance, originality, and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the manuscript's research relevance, originality, and contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize this assessment in the summary; decide early whether the work addresses an important question and adds new knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and alignment of conclusions with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate clarity of the writing and whether the manuscript's conclusions align with the presented evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag cases where conclusions overreach or contradict results; note language issues that impede comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and effectiveness of tables, figures, and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the effectiveness, clarity, and interpretability of tables, figures, and images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check labels, legends, readability, whether figures support claims, and whether data presentation is appropriate for the analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions contradicting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify where the manuscript's conclusions contradict or are not supported by the evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider such contradictions major flaws that may warrant rejection or major revision; give examples and point to specific results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outdated or unreliable methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect use of outdated, inappropriate, or unreliable methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend modern/appropriate methods or references; note methodological weaknesses that undermine results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlooked processes with known influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Spot omitted processes, variables, or controls known to influence the studied phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate missing experiments or considerations and how their omission affects conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient or contradictory data
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify data that are insufficient in quantity/quality or internally contradictory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why data are inadequate for the claims and what additional data or analyses are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological gaps affecting replicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify methodological gaps that prevent replication or undermine repeatability and robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for missing details (protocols, parameter values, software/code, data availability) and reference reporting standards (e.g., CONSORT) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial summary content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an initial summary in opening paragraphs that contextualizes the research question, methodology, and contribution to the field before deciding on rejection or further review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize strengths and main claims succinctly to orient editors and authors to your view of the manuscript's place in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-read detailed assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second read, refine assessment of argument construction, logical flow, clarity, title accuracy, abstract quality, and language issues affecting comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this pass to give specific, actionable suggestions on organization, rewriting, title/abstract improvements, and language edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: originality and necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Introduction should present the research argument and recent literature that establishes the study's originality and necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that background is up-to-date, frames the question clearly, and justifies the study's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials & Methods: replicability, robustness, and standards adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials and methods are described with sufficient detail for replicability, demonstrate robustness and repeatability, and adhere to relevant reporting standards (e.g., CONSORT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sample sizes, experimental conditions, statistical methods, ethical approvals, software and code availability, and any deviations from accepted standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results & Discussion: coherent narrative and appropriate analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that Results and Discussion present a clear, coherent narrative, include appropriate statistical analyses, and interpret findings in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analyses are correct and adequately reported (tests, effect sizes, uncertainty); verify interpretations do not overstate significance and are tied to results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions: evidence-based statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Conclusions are evidence-based and reflect the aims actually achieved by the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag speculative or overstated claims and request tempering of conclusions to match data.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: accuracy, adequacy, currency, and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess references for accuracy, adequacy, currency, and balance, avoiding over-reliance on self-citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check citation formatting and whether key relevant literature is cited, including recent work and alternative viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plausibility and presentation clarity of data and images and check for signs of undisclosed manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request raw data or higher-resolution images if needed; highlight any inconsistencies or potential manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure: Summary, Major issues, Minor issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the review report into a Summary (start with strengths and context), Major issues (flaws, severity, required revisions), and Minor issues (ambiguities, citation concerns, labeling errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with strengths, then list major problems with severity and required actions, followed by a concise list of minor/technical corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a recommendation (Accept, Revise, or Reject) accompanied by clear justifications and suggested improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending Revise, specify whether changes are major or minor and list concrete actions; if Rejecting, provide constructive pathways for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct principle
rubrics_metrics.description: "Treat the author's work the way you would like your own to be treated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive, fair, and professional in tone; prioritize actionable feedback that helps improve the manuscript.
